security_audit.summary: The static command-execution findings are false positives from Markdown backticks and Python code fences, not executable shell or Ruby code. The hardcoded URLs and system-reconnaissance detections are examples or resource links. One semantic issue remains: the async database example teaches SQL f-string interpolation and should use parameterized queries.

remediation.issue: Unsafe SQL string interpolation in the async database example.
remediation.suggestion: Use parameterized queries in every database example and state that untrusted input must never be formatted into SQL strings.

remediation.issue: Examples include public HTTP endpoints and placeholder API URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Clearly label network calls as illustrative examples and prefer placeholder domains unless live endpoints are required.

remediation.issue: Markdown code fences are being flagged as command execution by static analysis.
remediation.suggestion: No author security change is required, but scanner configuration should ignore Markdown fence delimiters for this skill type.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe SQL String Interpolation in Example
semantic_findings.description: The async database example builds SELECT queries with f-strings that include user_id. Readers could copy this pattern and create SQL injection risk if inputs are untrusted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 461-463 directly interpolate user_id into SQL text. The file is instructional, so the risk is unsafe guidance rather than active execution.

content.value_statement: Async Python code can be hard to structure, test, and debug. This skill provides patterns for asyncio, concurrency, timeouts, queues, rate limits, and async testing.
actual_capabilities: Explains asyncio core concepts, including event loops, coroutines, tasks, futures, and async iterators.
Shows practical patterns for await, gather, create_task, wait_for, and cancellation handling.
Demonstrates async context managers, queues, semaphores, locks, and producer-consumer workflows.
Provides examples for aiohttp scraping, simulated async database access, and WebSocket broadcasting.
Covers performance practices such as connection pools, batching, rate limits, and executor usage.
Includes testing guidance with pytest-asyncio and timeout assertions.
limitations: It is an educational Markdown skill, not an executable library or framework plugin.
Several examples use simulated clients, placeholder URLs, or simplified data models.
It does not provide full application scaffolds for FastAPI, aiohttp, or database drivers.
It does not profile running code or verify production performance automatically.

use_cases.title: Modernize I/O Workflows
use_cases.description: Convert sequential network, file, or database tasks into structured asyncio workflows with timeouts and cleanup.

use_cases.title: Design Concurrent Services
use_cases.description: Plan task orchestration, queue processing, and rate limiting for APIs, workers, and real-time services.

use_cases.title: Review Async Code Quality
use_cases.description: Check async code for missing awaits, blocking calls, weak cancellation handling, and unbounded concurrency.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Asyncio Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how event loops, coroutines, tasks, and await work in Python asyncio. Use simple examples and common mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Sequential I/O
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this sequential Python I/O workflow and propose an asyncio design using gather, timeouts, and clear error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design Bounded Concurrency
prompt_templates.scenario: Service owner handling external API limits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an async worker pattern for many API requests. Include semaphores, batching, retries, cancellation, and resource cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Async Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this async Python service for blocking calls, leaked tasks, missing cancellation paths, unsafe database access, and test gaps.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to fetch many URLs without overwhelming an API.
output: A bounded concurrency design using a semaphore and connection pool.
Timeout and error handling recommendations for each request.
Testing notes for success, timeout, and partial failure cases.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks why an async service sometimes stalls under load.
output: A checklist of blocking operations that may freeze the event loop.
Suggestions to move CPU-bound or blocking work into an executor.
Follow-up checks for cancellation, task leaks, and backpressure.

output_examples.input: A team wants a pattern for background jobs and async cleanup.
output: A producer-consumer structure with bounded queues and worker cancellation.
Guidance for context managers that close connections reliably.
Operational notes for rate limits, batching, and graceful shutdown.

best_practices: Use bounded concurrency, timeouts, and cancellation handling for all external I/O.
Prefer async context managers for resources that need deterministic cleanup.
Test async success paths, failures, timeouts, and cancellation behavior explicitly.
anti_patterns: Do not call blocking sleep, network, file, or database functions directly inside coroutines.
Do not create unbounded tasks for large input sets without backpressure.
Do not format untrusted values into SQL strings in async database code.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design async Python workflows that use asyncio, concurrent tasks, timeouts, queues, and resource cleanup.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete web service?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and review guidance that can be applied to services, workers, and scripts.

faq.question: Which Python features does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers async def, await, asyncio.run, gather, create_task, wait_for, queues, locks, semaphores, and async iterators.

faq.question: Can it help with aiohttp or FastAPI work?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes aiohttp examples and patterns that apply to async web frameworks such as FastAPI.

faq.question: Does it replace official asyncio documentation?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes practical patterns and should be used with official library documentation for exact API details.

faq.question: What should I review before using examples in production?
faq.answer: Review database parameterization, rate limits, authentication, retries, observability, and operational error handling.
